clue.text: Note produced by small musical instrument

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a harp is a stringed musical instrument

explanation.surface: A sound made by a little instrument, perhaps a piccolo or a toy harp.
explanation.definitionFit: A note raised by a semitone is called a sharp, so it names a kind of musical note.

clue.text: Cleric asks many questions before end of sacrament

parts.note: someone who pries is nosily asking lots of questions

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, here of sacrament

explanation.surface: A churchman quizzes people at length before the close of a religious rite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' simply puts the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A priest is an ordained minister of the church, a kind of clergyman.

clue.text: Partly open a glass container

parts.note: a jar is a glass container, for jam or pickles

explanation.surface: An instruction to open a glass container only a little way.
explanation.definitionFit: A door left slightly open is said to be standing ajar; the word is a straight synonym.

clue.text: Reptile quietly burrowing into ground

indicators.note: burrowing into means one piece digs its way inside the other

parts.note: terrain is the ground or land of an area
P (piano) is the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: A creature silently tunnelling into the earth.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrapin is a small freshwater turtle, and turtles are reptiles.

clue.text: After little time demand something to do

indicators.note: after means the demand comes after the time in the answer

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
to ask is to demand or require

explanation.surface: Shortly afterwards someone requests a job be done.
explanation.definitionFit: A task is a piece of work or a job, something one has to do.

clue.text: Mandela's regular newspaper spot, a capital feature

parts.note: Nelson Mandela was the South African statesman, so his possession is Nelson's
a column is a regular feature written in a newspaper

explanation.surface: Nelson Mandela's weekly piece in the paper, a highlight of the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: NELSON'S COLUMN is the monument to Admiral Nelson in Trafalgar Square, London; nothing to do with Mandela.
explanation.definitionFit: The monument is a famous landmark of London, the British capital.

clue.text: Have mishap when preparing vegetables, and own up

definitions.meaning: literally, to tip beans out by accident while cooking
to confess, to reveal a secret

explanation.surface: A cook knocks over the beans and then confesses to it.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to disclose a secret, while its literal reading is a kitchen accident with beans.

clue.text: Set of clothes, including large skirt

indicators.note: including means the clothes set holds the other piece inside

parts.note: kit is a set of clothing, such as football kit
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: An outfit that comes with an oversized skirt.
explanation.definitionFit: A kilt is a pleated knee-length skirt of tartan worn in Scottish dress.

clue.text: Unhappy beauty queen maybe cut flower

parts.note: feeling blue means feeling sad

indicators.note: cut means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a belle is a beautiful woman, the reigning beauty, perhaps a beauty queen

explanation.surface: A sad beauty pageant winner perhaps trims a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' removes the final E of BELLE, leaving BELL.
explanation.definitionFit: The bluebell is a woodland plant with blue bell-shaped blooms.

clue.text: Try jugged hare

indicators.note: jugged hare is a stewed dish, so the letters are stewed into a new order

explanation.surface: An invitation to taste a dish of stewed hare.
explanation.walkthrough: Jugged hare is a traditional British dish of hare stewed in a jug or casserole.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge tries a case, which is to hear it in court; a legal synonym.

clue.text: Weather in Chartres is terrible

indicators.note: in means the answer sits inside the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A complaint that the weather in the French city of Chartres is awful.
explanation.definitionFit: To weather a storm is to withstand it, so the verb means hold out against.

clue.text: Gosh! My sick pet's oddly missing

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters go missing, leaving the even ones of my sick pet's

explanation.surface: An exclamation of alarm because a poorly pet has disappeared.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of surprise or alarm.

clue.text: Very cold spell is liberating, so we're told

indicators.note: so we're told signals what is heard rather than what is written

parts.note: frees up means liberates or releases

explanation.surface: A cold snap that, reportedly, sets people free.
explanation.definitionFit: A freeze-up is a period of extreme frost when water and roads become frozen.

clue.text: Put up with whiskers being trimmed

indicators.note: trimmed means the word has its final letter clipped off

parts.note: a beard is a growth of whiskers on the face

explanation.surface: Tolerating facial hair while it gets a trim.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear something is to tolerate or endure it.

clue.text: Make quick progress in top set, after revision

indicators.note: revision means the letters of in top set are revised into a new order

explanation.surface: A pupil advances fast in the top class after revising for exams.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is an urging to hurry, to go faster, as when telling a driver to accelerate.

clue.text: The last word in Lamentations

indicators.note: in means the answer sits inside the letters of the next word

explanation.surface: The final word of the biblical Book of Lamentations.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the word that closes prayers and hymns, literally the final word spoken.

clue.text: Sort of tense and unwell? Start to eat throat lozenge

parts.note: the past is one kind of grammatical tense
ill means unwell

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, here of eat

explanation.surface: Feeling strained and poorly, someone begins eating a cough sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastille is a small medicated sweet sucked to soothe a sore throat.

clue.text: Platform is supporting US lawyer

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits beneath the lawyer

parts.note: DA is a District Attorney, a public prosecutor in the United States

explanation.surface: A stage is backing an American attorney.
explanation.definitionFit: A dais is a raised platform at one end of a hall, for speakers or a top table.

clue.text: Lone royalist struggling

indicators.note: struggling means the letters of royalist thrash about into a new order

explanation.surface: A single supporter of the monarchy fighting on alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean alone, existing or acting without others.

clue.text: Draughts in the PM's weekend home

definitions.meaning: the board game also called checkers
the country house in Buckinghamshire used by the British Prime Minister

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister plays a board game at their country retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: Draughts is the British name for checkers.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the board game's alternative name; the other is the official country residence of Britain's Prime Minister.

clue.text: Ill-considered advice to reduce babysitting commitments?

definitions.meaning: split into two words, it tells someone to look after children less often

explanation.surface: Telling a babysitter to take on fewer jobs is foolish advice.
explanation.definitionFit: Something thoughtless or careless is done without using the brain at all.

clue.text: Concept that's almost perfect

indicators.note: almost means the word stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: ideal means perfect

explanation.surface: A notion that is nearly flawless.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean a thought or notion formed in the mind.

clue.text: Reserve something from the library

definitions.meaning: to make a ... for a seat or table
a volume one can borrow from a library

explanation.surface: Asking the library to set aside a volume for you.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to make a reservation, and the noun is a printed volume one borrows.

clue.text: Broken piece of work by sculptor

definitions.meaning: a sculpture of the head and shoulders

explanation.surface: A sculptor's statue that has been smashed.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang uses the word for something broken; in art it is a sculpted head and shoulders.
